reviewsWithKeywords.text: No rocks, just sand and really good restaurant nearby. It was crowded even with the big beach but can still swim freely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come early to avoid the crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches are still beautiful and clean, but the north part of the island is way overpopulated. We even went to stay during the week and still find lot of tourists.Lot of business in the beaches selling food, restaurants, chairs, umbrellas from the hotels. Then you have the boats coming from Cancun with lot of "party" people, putting loud music and park just right there next to the beach. Can't imagine all the trash that this beautiful beach is getting underground.If you like to enjoy some privacy in the beach, then this island is not for you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Norte area is great for swimming in the ocean. There are umbrellas chairs and foodShowers. The sun was hot drink lots of water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chill/beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really beautiful and nice beach but small space to swim. The chairs and sunbrellas are only 200 pesos per person so it pays off to rent some. Also bring beer/drinks with you with a freezer from Oxxo :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous As Always
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best sand. Most clear and calm water. Heaven. Great beach clubs, food & drink choices, and massages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best part of ANY island! Playa Norte is the best! On the North side gets a little warm as the breeze is minimal. Around the corner on the West side you get a fabulous breeze as you watch the sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches we have been to in all our years of traveling.  Super soft sand and calm water with the best colors.  It’s a must see if you go to isla.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is a great place to relax, have some beer and then a relaxing massage. I’m happy happy happy with Isla Mujeres

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach with some cool restaurants on it. The water is super warm!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is beautiful with calm waters. Many restaurants on the beach, water is very warm and a beautiful color

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach around
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is an amazing beach near town and you can venture out100 yds and still be up to your waiste in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but crowded with party boats
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really nice... but unfortunately during the day some boats are coming from Cancun and they party all day long from the boats. All the jetski and the loud music break the charm of that beach. Worst of it... they don't leave a cent of money on the island... real shame...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spring Break 2021
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this place. Family friendly but Adult fun. Beautiful spot, lots of food and drink options. Close to town but fairly secluded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is always wonderful here, in April the water is fairly cool unlike when visiting in the months of July or August. I highly recommend bringing along a dry bag large enough for your belongings so you can just walk from the beach into the water without worrying about leaving your belongings behind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world, but TOO MANY BOATS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been to Playa Norte probably 20 times or more in my life since the mid 90’s. It is an absolutely beautiful beach with shallow, turquoise waters, flour-like white sand and little to no seaweed. It has always been more crowded over the past couple of years but this year was substantially worse. By far, the worst part is that there are now a large number of boats and yachts that come to the beach and drop anchor just past the swimming barrier. This is the first time that I have seen this, maybe a newer thing since Covid? Not sure. A lot of them blast music so people on the beach and swimmers are forced to listen to several different boat’s music all at once, not fun. Also, the boats really ruin the view for the beach goers. Still a beautiful beach, but something needs to be done about this issue, especially the noise. I counted around 20 boats on weekdays and close to 50 on Friday and Saturday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s crowded but a beautiful stretch of beach. We stayed on the other side of the island but enjoyed day trips to old town and Playa Norte!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the nicest beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like really loud music, sitting 2 feet from the person next to you, during COVID, not good, how is this allowed???  and not very clear water, you will like this place.We went on Sunday to try it. The Ferry ride over was great and fun. Then we walked to the beach. We were so disappointed because we read such good reviews. The water is not crystal clear and very cloudy and the beach clubs has obnoxious people playing very loud music, so if you want to sit on a beach and relax, it's impossible.  One guy had a boombox playing very loud rock and roll. Do you really want to sit next to this guy. Do you think the patrons of the beach club would tell him to turn down the volume. No. So this place is for people who like all of above. We went around the corner and the water was lovely, the beach wasn't that crowded and it was way better than Playa Norte. They need to change a few things there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm, gorgeous water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is perfect for swimming or lounging in the sun on the sand. The beach is so clean... no seaweed, and super calm, cool turquoise water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful and the people are all in festive vibe to have wonderful time. Some of the best sunsets will be seen from playa Norte. Enjoy the views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach soft sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful, soft sand, clear water, only thing I didn't like is all boats who dock close by, otherwise it's a paradise

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and water -- looks just like the pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand is powder soft and bright white. The water is SO turquoise blue, and quite  shallow. We would lay out in the sun, then dip in for a refreshing swim. There are plenty of bars and restaurants all up & down the beach. Sometimes, you might get a waiter or a local person who approaches you to see if you'll come eat at the restaurant or buy some trinkets from them. But they are not pushy at all, and you just have to say "No, thank you". It didn't bother me at all.You will notice there are many boats anchored just a little offshore in the middle of the day, bringing people over from Cancun for the afternoon. There is plenty of room for everybody though - we always found a good spot to be away from crowds.- It was a great way to spend our first three days on Isla Mujeres -

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on ISLA!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hands-down the best beach on isla! We stayed at privileges alux and we’re hanging out at their beach club but could walk around the point anytime we wanted absolutely stunning view amazing water great vendors all along the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden Paradise in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my favorite part of the whole vacation! It is stunningly beautiful! TIP: Go to the far north east side to find the little lagoon. The lagoon is full of little fish and the water is so clear/blue that you can see them swimming around. The sand is so soft. It feels like you are dreaming. If you are going to Isla you cannot pass this up!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love it!  Great beginner snorkel place.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Snorkeled here for a few hours while our taxi waited for us.  Thankfully we brought our own gear as I didn't see any rental places.  Water was crystal clear but the waves were crashing hard on the reef so view wasn't great.  We did see a lot of fish, but nothing too amazing.Current through from the bay to the sea was fast and dangerous but there was a lifeguard standing there keeping a close eye on that spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: INCREDIBLE BEACH - the party scene
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is gigantic with some great bars for some outstanding people watching. It is rated one of the top 10 beaches in the world and it is.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This place is beautful day or night!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been to Isla Mujeres many times over the years for day trips, this was my first time staying on the island.  My husband and I had a magical walk on the beach one evening, the moon was bright and it was simply stunning.  I hope to be back soon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach area just a bit crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Here comes all the people from Cancun, and also everyone will visit from the island stayers. definitely worth it! Just saying that there are several boats parking in front of the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white sands, tranquil, crystal blue water! Definitely worth the excursion from downtown Isla Mujeres.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I did not stay at or near the beach but we travel here by gulf cart to enjoy the beautiful blue water and excellent beach from our hotel which was near the south of the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water is amazing and beach is beautiful.  It was quite busy the day we went but we still enjoyed it.  Stopped at the bar with swings right at the entrance to have a margarita before continuing our day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sugar sand. Blue kool-aid looking water. Perfect slope and sand in the water. Clarity and cleanliness of water is off the charts. Yachts and ferries sailing by. And a perfect island vibe! Can’t wait to go back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING FOOD
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love this place & always stop in while in Isla Mujeres. They’re expanding to accommodate even more people. Worth the wait!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Norte....A Beautiful & Calm Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is the perfect beach for kids.  The waters are such a beautiful shade of turquoise, clear, and extremely calm.  Parents will definitely not have to worry about waves crashing into their very young children.  Also, if you child is old enough this is the perfect spot for beginning snorkeling.  If you are staying at Mia Reef there are paddle boards and kayaks to use free of charge.  Playa Norte is also wonderful for just relaxing and enjoying the simple life.  Please note that there are many day trips to Playa Norte from Cancun so the beach has the potential to become crowded but that was not a problem for us during our visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches are beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hidalgo street is a tourist trap and try to avoid after first pass. Several good restaurants and a couple of great street vendors. Not much to see or do.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect sand and water though a bit chilly.  Go in the morning and there is plenty of room and empty chairs before the crowds arrive after noon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but......
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many other reviews have said that the beach has narrowed over the years. We didn’t find it too narrow and had plenty of sand to walk over to get to the sun beds provided by our hotel (the Ixchel - highly recommended) but it was surprisingly busy, given travel restrictions these days. There were plenty of bars, restaurants and services (watercraft, massages etc) around but, most noticeably, a lot of boats (presumably on day trips from Cancún) are anchored just off the beach all day, some playing music very loudly. Very nice water for swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the nicest in the whole Maya Riviera.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, lots of visitors, soft white sand. Even during a pandemic, you almost forget about it when visiting this slice of Paradise. Don't miss this beach if you come to Isla Mujeres. One of the nicest in the whole Maya Riviera.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous public beach, did not have a lot of seaweed while we were there. The pic is a view of it from our resort.  Lots of fun bars and restaurants along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach, just about 10 min walk from the ferry.  Many shops and restaurants around.  The north side is very nice and smooth. To the north you find more waves. They have several massages tables around for relaxation.  The water is clear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded place, waiters just wanna get people for their umbrellas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Isla is dirty and smelly. MX$300 for an umbrella in Playa Norte. The day we went there were lots of people on the sand and on boats with loud music near the beach. Color of the water is impressive though, but wouldn't go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach On Isla
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best swimmable beach on Isla (Best Scenic Beach is Punta Sur). Nice soft white sand, clear waters, and turquoise hues. Definitely must go here. :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top place to stay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is by far the best spot on the whole island. You are close to the center, you have good options and good swing bars. There is something for everyone here and during the summer the water is so calm you just chill in the water with a cold drink in your hand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven or Hell
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No question asked Playa Norte is beautiful and there is plenty of room for everyone here but our personal experience from staying on the beachfront hotel for 5 days is that the beach has 2 different faces; beautiful and tranquil paradise during the first part of the day and then it becomes a music club for boats with drunk and loud parties spoiling it until about 5-6PM when finally almost all of them go back to Cancun/mainland - pretty sad but that is the reality (and we visited during pretty slow COVID November 2020...)There are numerous beach clubs to rent chairs from and some decent food options if you don't want to leave the beach at all - do your homework as they are somewhat placed in different areas and they do feel differently. The area by Mia Hotel has the most sand bars, the middle is fewer building and more palm trees and the corner where ChiChi's 'n Charlies is where you will find more building on the waterfront - the range of spots where you can stay is pretty great :)Great beach for swimming in peaceful waters, walk on sandbars and enjoy the views, and sunsets :) we loved taking a stroll from one end to the end in the evening when things started to calm down but I must say after 2-3 days the loudness of it gets a bit annoying - do try Playa Centro (next door on the west coast) as boats don't go there and the waters are pretty nice as well.TIP: many beach clubs take credit cards, also many have deals actually where after spending certain amount the beach chair and umbrellas become freeTIP: lots of vendors selling cigars, hats etc. just be nice and politely say no if you aren't interested, just be prepared to be asked a lot of times :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach with calmer waters than some of the beaches in the hotel zone of Cancun. There are plenty of bars along the water if you want to get a drink or a bite to eat

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful Beach! Plenty of fun and sun! A lot of entrepreneurs selling things but they didn’t hound you if you said no! Place where the boats dock. Music and a good time!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good beach overall. Basically next to the Ixchel Beach Hotel and as you walk out of the hotel you are at the beach. It can get kinda crowded though so that is something to be mindful of.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach yet!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach I have ever visited.  The water was muy fresca and felt amazing all day everyday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach daydreams are made of!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most BEAUTIFUL beach I have visited so far in my life! It’s clear and every beautiful shade of blue you can imagine. We absolutely love swimming there and laying out on the beach. It’s the very essence of true paradise! I could look at that water forever...😍😭

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesoooome Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is one of my favorite places/beaches in the world! The water is so crystal clear and calm you don’t even want to get out of the water! It’s just so beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Again and again!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are uncertain about what beach to visit on your trip to Cancun or Riviera Maya look no more!Playa Norte has an expansive beach with clear waters and no waves, so perfect for everyone. Plus sunsets are quite something.Also, it never gets seaweed, so when everything is packing that algae, you could still swim here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow, what a beautiful beach and location.  We found a small bar ocean front and were able to enjoy the water for a few hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one of the most beautiful beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been a permanent world traveler for about 2 years, and have seen some amazing beaches. between the solitude, and the water color, plus the easy access to the city itself, and of course shade! gives this a big thumbs up

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Closed due to Covid but..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So the beach is currently closed because of Covid but we ended up going to a bar along the beach and ordering margaritas and they let us stay and swim and we had no problems at all. The sand is very nice, the beach very clean and we didn’t see any algae in the water which was great. Very beautiful, blue beach and I’d say it’s worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best side of the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beaches are beautiful - but dont expect waves, the ocean is very calm at this part of the island - perfect for families and small children. Lots of great options for food and drinks!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: CURRENTLY CLOSED
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is CURRENTLY CLOSED TO EVERYONE. This beach is absolutely beautiful, however it's closed - even the private areas owned by hotels/restaurants are inaccessible and they have people policing it. We didn't know this before booking our hotel. The other beaches further south on the island are open, it's just Playa Norte and Playa Centro.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: turquoise waters the best ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: WHAT A LOVELY PLACE, the turquoise waters are amazing. A MOST IN THE CARIBBEAN. The white sand and the open sky, unique experience to enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A place to reflect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: North shore is a must in isla mujeres. Try watching  sundown or watch the sun come up! I have visited many times and everytime is a new experience. The beach does not change much, clear blue water with gentle waves and white sand beaches.... what is a bit different is me. I love to reflect as I look.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Closed.  Water Open.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is so dumb.  If you are staying on North Beach you can't walk on the beach.  If you hire a party boat out of Cancun you can use the water in front of the beach.  Here is a picture of the boat traffic using the water in front of the beach.  They are literally lined up up from the top to the bottom of the beach.  But you can't touch the sand if you staying here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing view and ocean is crystal clear
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing view and restaurant that’s located at the location has a breath taking and relaxing view. Prices are not that expensive and food was delicious.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Attraction to visit on golf cart
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The island is just 7 kilometer road.    You can rent a golf cart for 4 people for 150 pesos per hour (8 dlls per hour) or "negotiate a better deal for 3 or 4 hour.    You drive around and stop on any place to enjoy the nice sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Sandy Beaches!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The north beach is very beautiful and also crowded but well worth visiting for the day.  You can rent beach chairs at one of the many establishments on the beach and get food/refreshments served to you at your beach chair or go up and sit at their restaurant.  Get there early for a good spot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful blue water! We walked the beach but then sat at a bar right at the edge of the water and had drinks, it was like the Corona commercials.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is a must stop!  The water is amazing and the sand is soft and white.  We ventured there for sunset and were not disappointed.  It was truly a sensational place to watch the sun set.  We have also visited in the daytime and usually it is very busy with a vibrant atmosphere!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, can get crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, clean (when we were there), and friendly. It can get crowded.The water is beautiful and it is a nice place to relax for a few hours. We enjoy watching the boats as they anchor, come by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, powdery sand, but way too busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous, but we found it terribly over-crowded. Large groups were leaving their garbage behind everywhere, and we found it hard to take in the beauty with the place being so overrun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with turquoise water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed this amazing beach with the turquiose water and white sand!! Dont miss it! Great for spending 2-3 hours

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tourist Mecca and sandy beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gobbled up with the Mia Reef resort at the pit and resorts at most of the beaches, you can still sneak into on of the restaurants which has sandy beaches.  Try Playa Centro a public beach with swim areas.  Chair and umbrella rentals run a bit pricey.  Coco Restaurant and Beach Bar is chill with great service.  Beachside massages are also available.  Most everyone speaks English, but try and speak their native Spanish and you will gain a friend and respect.  Lots of street vendors and places to rent golf carts to tour the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Halloween and Dia de Los Muertos in Playa Norte
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unlike many places in Mexico right now, Isla Mujeres is pretty safe for tourists, especially if you stay in Playa Norte along the areas around Hidalgo, a no-car street lined with bars, restaurants and tourist shops. Cheesy? Yes. A little like Bourbon St meets Duval St? You betcha. Worth spending a few nights there? Absolutely. Check out Las Brisas Mexicanos on Hidalgo and Matamoros for the best Enchiladas with Salsa Verde I’ve every had (it’s the Salsa Verde) and don't miss El Patio down the road for the live music. There’s an incredible local band that does all 80s and 90s rock, and fantastic drinks too (cash only). At the end of the night sit on a swing  and enjoy a margarita outside Stingray’s (Hidalgo and Mateos), and then get fresh churros from Churrasic Park, a vendor right on the corner.  The end of October is a lot of fun on Isla Mujeres. On Halloween, local children trick or treat through the area and it’s really a cute sight. If you make it to one of the Dia de los Muertos festivals around the central plaza, there’s food, music and traditional costumes and religious displays. It’s so worth checking it out. Don’t stop with just Hidalgo and Playa Norte though, rent a golf cart (they’re cheaper in town than at most resorts) and drive all over. There’s great views at Punta Sur (the southern point of the island) and friendly people throughout.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most luxurious beach I have ever enjoyed.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Soft white sand that doesn’t burn your feet. The Mia Reef Resort is on its own island beside Isla Mujeres which causes a rapid flow of current between the two. The water is mostly shallow so there is no danger. Once you float out to the rope that stops you, there is deep water but if you keep going it gets shallow again. There is plenty of shallow water for kids to enjoy a swim. Frigate birds are soaring overhead all day- amazing. It’s a safe area to swim, keeping in mind the sun is very hot, there is no shade, and the wind makes you think you are not getting burned. I got burned on several days, no matter what shirt or screen I put on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nautibeach beach club is my new love
reviewsWithKeywords.text: North Beach is always a must but this was my first time at Nautibeach. Great service, the food is spectacular and the drinks are beyond spectacular. That was my first time at Nautibeach and it will not be my last. The sand is so soft. The water is perfect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Norte
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach! The waist deep water in the lagoon is perfect to float in! It’s busy during the middle of the day but we’ll worth a trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing cristal water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see! Beautiful beach! Not much free space as lots of beach club along the beach.But Loved it!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is like paradise on earth. White sand and turquoise waterBeautiful! Planning to go back and I left yesterday!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented a golf cart and found street parking easily. We took sandwiches and a cooler from our AirB&B and enjoyed the day at the beach. We were there on a Sunday and it was very crowded. I would recommend Central beach as it seemed to have more room for our chairs we also brought. Can easily rent beach chairs and umbrellas on both beaches. Vendors walked by from time to time selling ice cream bars, fresh fruit and bracelets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Grab a parking spot for your golf cart, rent a beach chair and enjoy! Lots of good beach restaurants to enjoy. Most of the other beaches are not free.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the prettiest beaches you will ever see! Can get crowded, but still worth the view. Tons of beach bars around also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the prettiest beaches I have ever seen. Gorgeous shallow water, soft white sand, plenty of spots to spend the day on a blanket or in a lounge chair.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Isla Mujeres
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach in Isla Mujeres and the best option if taken others into comparison. Although swimming restrictions were very high (limited space to swim), this beach was mostly calm and safe to spend a part of the day whilst visiting the island. Upon arrival, we saw many restaurants and bars, as well as various lounge chairs and sun canopies displayed along the sand. It can get a bit crowed at some times of the day, but it is definitely a must see. This beach is really close to the pier head, so walking here is not a big deal. Customer service at the bars and restaurants surrounding the beach was really good, and best time to sit and have some food should certainly be during sunset hours. They have awesome local beers and surprisingly food was top quality. Pictures taken here were the best ones. Everyone should come visit and have a dip in the beautiful sea here. It's wonderful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great breakfast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Coconut French toast was as good as all the reviews say!! A must try. Next time the eggs Benny which looked amazing as well

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day at the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach.  Easy to get to off the ferry and downtown.  Gets crowded at times, especially on Sundays.  Go early to get beach chairs or cabanas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Trip to Isla 2020
reviewsWithKeywords.text: CrowdedHectic NoisyCrowdedTequila soakedIntoxicated Touristy Perfect if you're under 40A lot of fun if you're in the right frame of mind!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, sand and warm water. You can lay on your own towel or rent an umbrella and lounger. Drinks are served beach side and are reasonably priced.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most stunning beaches!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're traveling to Isla Mujeres this is the place to be.  Head to the furthest north/west tip of the island for the best beach area, it's nice and shallow and you can walk out forever in the calm aqua waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great beach with turquoise water. A must see on Isle Mujures. We rented a bed with an umbrella at a local restaurant and had a nice day. Great beach to walk!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach. Well worth a visit. Lots of places to eat, drink and shop nearby. A highlight of our trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach from Isla Mujeres. Clear water, nice people, cold drinks. This is the beach that you must visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous overcrowded beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful - and I do mean gorgeous - beach but way overcrowded with chairs and cabanas that you need to  purchase . Great place if your looking to party with a crowd.  Get there early or later in the evening (bring the deet) for a really great beach experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is as beautiful as everyone says.  The water was amazing.  Lots of people and very busy on the weekend.  Tuesday wasn't as busy and we enjoyed it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach that’s gotten too busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach that’s just too busy!! Says it all Guess it depend on when you’re here! Too many people on top of one another... other side of the island is more attractive at least to us now...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is a must!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach with calm waters! The beach gets busy by noon, we would recommend getting a chair at a resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Slice of Heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is our 8th year on the island and we come for the weather, beach and food.  It's a nice place to be in February.  Beautiful white sand and Carribean Blue water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great sandy bottom, nice swimming, lots of people and boats. You must rent a chair and umbrella if your going to be there a full day. lots of venders.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: North Beach Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: North Beach was once pristine and lovely,  but it has grown to be too crowded.  Some days it is difficult to find a spot.  In recent years, massage huts, beach clubs, vendors and bars/restaurants have taken over much of the space.  There are only a few areas where you can go to set up your own chairs or blanket without having to rent lounges or order overpriced food and drinks to sit at a beach club.  I have often counted 50 boats anchored off of North Beach, many of which play loud music.  There is a  constant parade of boats coming from  Cancun loaded with snorklers to snorkel in waist deep water in the bay.  It is best to visit the beach in the morning or to come later in the day.  Midday is too crazy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water is crystal clear beautiful. Tiny waves which id great for swimming and for little ones. The sand is so sift and white

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach / Great Sorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A visit to  Isla Mujuers ..should  include  Playa Norte ! Nice swimable beach. Beaches in the hotel zone much more beautiful. Downside is  that it is commercial ,crowded and no where to park .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: GORGEOUS!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It tooks us alllllll day to get here because we somehow bought the wrong ferry trip to Isla Mujeres, BUT - it was worth it once we got to Playa Nortew!!! The water is the most beautiful color and super calm, so it is great for the little ones. I wish we had more time here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: very crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place is very crowded and there is not a lot of space to stay except if you pay for a chair. The view is beatifull but not amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: "North Beach" area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very crowded with chase lounges right up to water line. Some seaweed issues as some areas do not rake up and move away. If you want the loud, beach, party scene this is it on the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach’n It
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bring your towel, chairs , cooler or whatever you can carry!  Just pick an out of the way shady spot and setup shop. No need to rent a chaise unless you want to. Lots of people watching. Get wet and stay cool under a shade tree if you can find it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Annoying Beach People
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to a public beach on Playa Norte.  Was very nice shallow waters with white soft sand. I've been spoiled seeing countless beaches around the world so this was OK for me.  Not spectacular but nice. Unfortunately  MXN dude approaches us and  is insisting that we pay 400 MXN pesos ($30 CND) for a lounger that we were not using.  We had our own blanket and umbrella.  He went and got another friend from a restaurant and both of them tried bullying us off the beach and kept saying we cant use our umbrella.  After about 15 mins pestering us I told him it is a public beach! Unless he showed me in writing a law that states we can not use our own umbrella and blanket then back off or call the PoPo.  After that he left us alone.  Unfortunately Quintana Roo, Mexico has become very expensive.  No one is starving. No beggers. No homeless, which is a good thing but at the great expense of the touristas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is, by far, the best beach on the island. There are multiple options for accommodations or beach club rental on this end of the island.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter vacation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place for breakfast or lunch. People working treat you like family. Great Bloody Mary’s. We have eaten several breakfast there and have never been disappointed. Will go back. Cute place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Catamaran to Isla Mujeres was great!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took a trip to the island and walked to Playa Norte, incredible sight! went swimming in unbelievable water it was an amazing experience! The water was so clear and pretty calm- all the little shops and people selling on the streets was amazing as well. Was the best part of our trip by far

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful! Bring Pesos!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Made me want to stay the night here, so I did! The area is so fun, the water is gorgeous and clean! 300 pesos to rent a beach chair, great price!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous sand and water. Walk around before settling in - there are definitely quieter and busier sections of the beach. Pros - free, byob, beautiful sand and water, sandy bottom.  Cons - can get busy and loud (music coming from speakers in all directions lol), Centro gets busy with tour boats

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One word - Awesome
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you make it to Isla Mujeres a must. Plenty of places to chill or hang for the day. Walking distance to downtown, dining and entertainment if needed. Plenty of places to rent water toys, chairs, etc. If a need just ask someone always willing to help. Remember beach ettitique is important and pick up after self. Enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful white sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A spacious beach covered in a beautiful white sand.  Take along a towel and enjoy the water.  Easy access.  We all appreciated the chance to relax after a long walk from the opposite end of he island which I also recommend.  You will have to rent a chair and umbrella if you want one but will make your stay more comfortable if you have a little shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing Relaxing Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing white sand beach! Crystal clear Beautiful turquoise water teeming with aquatic life. No waves just smooth as glass.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sand and ocean with no sea weed.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is and outstanding beach.  We spent as many days as possible swimming and laying in sun here.  It is expensive if you aren't staying at a resort with their own beach chairs.  It was 300 pesos minimum to rent a table and plastic chairs.  Some areas of this beach are close to ferry and boat traffic.  Stay until the sun sets, its breathtaking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top quality beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice sand, quality water and had a place on the beach...beautiful location. Have been there twice for 10 days and likely to go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in Isla Mujeres!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is my favorite spot in Isla Mujeres. The beach is nice and safe. You can literally walk some meters and you'll find hundreds of fish. It's a great place for snorkeling. Really, you don't even need to swim. Amazing experience!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach on the Island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All water areas on the Island are beautiful, this beach is the most tranquil, busy but floatable. Everything you need can be gotten here, massages, food and shopping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an amazing breach. We rented a golf cart and drove here to spend a few hours. We ordered foot and drinks and just played in the water. Bring a beach blanket and water. Enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everyone we asked and everywhere we read mentioned how Playa Norte is a must. We arrived to the island around 9:30 and walked to Playa Norte (about 10 minutes). It was practically empty. We walked around some more and swam in the crystal clear water. Around 111, it started to get more packed. The beach is clean and there is plenty of space to put your towel down and tan.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pure tranquility
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There really is no place like Playa Norte. Beautiful, tranquil, and one of the best places in all of the Caribbean to catch a sunset. We always go to Tarzan’s and grab a table. Cost are an expensive and the sunset can’t be beat

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This public beach is a great place to spend the day. Parking is a little tough, but take your time and you’ll get a spot. There were tons of boats anchored at the beach and the people camped out on the beach for the day. We brought our snorkel gear and checked out the grassy/rocky area by the hotel on the Northeast end. Honestly, the water was so clear and there were so many fish right in the shallow area that we didn’t even need our snorkel gear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place for the kids to play
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super fun to play in the currents, snorkel around the rocks, or play in the warm shallow waters. Public beach! There are plenty of beach front restaurants/clubs to order food/drinks/chairs but you can bring your own for the fraction of the cost and enjoy your day just the same

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at privilege aluxes, which was right around the corner from Playa Norte. Love, love this beach. Clean, clear water. Great people watching.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Catamaran day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Food. Ambiance. All of it is amazing The personnel is friendly, the place is clean and the food is delicious

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fabulous beach on Isla Mujeres with restaurants all around so you don't need to go far.  We stayed on the Island for a 5 day/4 night family vacation and loved it all!  Highly recommend with beautiful sunrises & sunsets.  You get them both on this island!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beaches, crystal clear water. We did not stay on this island just a day visit, we would definitely return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach, lots of selfies
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach overall.  Nice for swimming. Small for the number of people trying to hang out there. I would prefer a slightly less crowded beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful white sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the premier beach of Isla Mujeres and every hotel has a bar and/or restaurant right on this beach.  Best times are earlier in the morning or later in he afternoon after the day trippers go home.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: GORGEOUS!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white sand & calm turquoise water. We didn't rent a chair or umbrella, just towels on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Like the old days
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of our best experiences South was Playa Mujeres.  Still has the narrow cobblestone streets that cars don’t fit down and you can walk everywhere.  Sit and have a beer at a cantina and watch life go by. The highlight of the day trip was playa Norte.  Take a towel and a cooler and sit in the sand and swim in the clear warm sea.  It’s like the 80s when all beaches were public and you just bought a chair from a vendor or brought your own.  We made like hippies all day, sun swimming and cervesas.  Just walk if your at all mobile.  Don’t waste money on a golf carts.  Turn left from the ferry, walk to the end of the road and your there.  About a 5 minute stroll.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Winter get a way
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice relaxed atmosphere. Very laid back. Norte beach is quite shallow and you can walk out in the ocean a long way in shallow warm water. Very clear and soft white sand. Hotels facing the beach had very crowded lounges. The first 50 yards in from the water is a public beach and the resorts property continued in from there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best island !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best island i have been to, a very small one with coast to coast 2-3 minutes walk at the narrowest point, beautiful clear blue water. going to Isla Mujeres should be a must when visiting Cancun

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm Blue Water!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent every day over the holidays at Playa Norte.  The water seemed warmer this time of year than last year.  It felt like when we visit at the end of May.  There was some erosion since this summer, but realize the sand shifts.  There was a little sargassum at times (nothing much) after rain storms.  This is still are favorite place to hang out each day.  We prefer to spend our time at Mayan Beach Club since it doesn't get as crowded there as other parts of the beach (Ixchel to MIA).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: January at Playa Norte
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is truly one of the best beaches in the world.  The water is clear and blue and the sand is white and perfect for a beach day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrun with tourists but pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: North Beach is great because the water is most always calm and shallow enough to swim.  Unfortunately, they are way over crowded with tourists these days.  If you want to relax, the other side of North beach just South of Playa Mia is lest tourists but you can't always swim over there because of current.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and water but I wasn't expecting it to be so built up.  Entire beach is lined with bars, restaurants and rental chairs /umbrellas. Completely packed with tours the day we went.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean beach but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walkable from the ferry.  Can snorkel from the beach. Sand is soft and a great place to picnic. Parking is tough in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view. Water is crystal clear. Sand is so soft. Water does not get deep anywhere we went. It gets very crowded. Get there early if you want a seat on the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated, crowded and highly commercialised
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Better beaches elsewhere on the island. Too many commercial establishments / restaurants do not give a relaxing feel... I found cancun hotel zone beach better. Kids refused to enter water as they did not find it appealing enough..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful calm water. Soft fine sand.  Crowded but this is a busy time of year, last week a December, first of Jan.   Hotel properties are closing in on beachfront.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa norte beach - beautiful blue water and nice views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is the north end of the island and it is one of the best beaches which has amazing landscapes, affordable and great for kids with amazing shades of blue water. Remember to apply sunscreen as you will get tan in a few hours. This beach was enjoyed by all age groups and water is very shallow, towards the end there are some rocks and a small house with nice views.There is a lot of opportunities for shopping, dining/bars with music, spas/massages, local tours, and snorkeling. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach around the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is a beach at the north end of the island, is is beautiful but the clubs around it , takes advantage of it’s beautiful by there prices

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white soft sand, amazing shades of blue water, and incredible snorkeling opportunities.Wade into the calm warm water then take a nap on the warm soft sand while the sun caresses you into dreams of paradise.This beach has something for every age. Just remember your sunscreen because you will want to stay all-day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa norte review
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean beach, amazing landscape,spacious, affordable and great for kids because the sea is like a pool

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach and places to snorkel out in the water.  It is a great place for kids as the water is very shallow for quit a ways out.  There is also a nice place to walk to some rocks and a small house.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm clear water, soft sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is absolutely beautiful and the island is so small that you can easily walk to neighboring beaches along the water for a change of scenery.  The swimming section does not extend very far in the ocean due to boat crossings but there is still enough space to swim around and enjoy the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very good experience to go on Playa Norte beach!! I really recommend it . There are plenty of things to do like feed fish ,listen to Discotheque music and just swim around without any waves ! Water is absolutely beautiful and not too crowded!!! Nice place for food and drinks too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the beach here even though it was so windy. Go all the way to the bridge to The resort to see the whole area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: White sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First came to this place 31 years ago for honeymoon. Its alot more crowded now and more built up but it's still the best beach on the island and one of my favs. Lots to see, eat, drink and do here. The one annoyance is the vendors selling everything that keep approaching you. Dont even look at them and they just keep walking. The turquoise color of the ocean is gorgeous

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach around!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is by far the best beach...water was absolutely beautiful and not too crowded!  Nice place there for food and drinks as well.  Sarcasm was there but didn't interfere with anything...great for wading...plus a sandbar,.  This beach is perfect for those traveling with children of all ages...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best beach of the island! Warm turquoise water, white beachWell frequented! Good restaurants with an extremely good service To come back  Unforgettable

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good people watching
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed a few sunny hours on the beach at Playa Norte.  We parked our golf cart nearby and brought our own blanket and snacks, so didnt need to rent a chair or use bar services.  We found pleasantly clean, soft sand and warm waves.  It was somewhat crowded and a little noisy, but not too bad.  There are a few vendors, similar to everywhere we have been in Cancun. Quite a bit of boat traffic with the ferries and party boats passing quite close.  Nice beach here,  but i think we have been spoiled during our stay at Casa Maya so it didn't seem spectacular to us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded but pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love the powder sands of Playa. Its getting more and more crowded every time I go. Wish it could be kept a secret!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in the world.  Busy though.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can walk into the open ocean forever. Beach chairs can be rented for US$15 for the day, however, you can also just leave  your stuff on the beach. Very shallow.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is gorgeous. No filters needed. Shallow. Lots to see when snorkeling. No heavy currents or undertows. It is a must see!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach and the water is gorgeous. Worth a visit while on Isla Mujeres. We took the ferry over from Playa Tortuagas for a day trip. We rented a golf cart to cruise around the island. We visited Playa Norte to relax on the beach for a bit and go swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stayed at Mia reef
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was beautiful. The beach is private but public can access the waters but most don’t. There’s a reef and plenty to look at if you like to snorkel. The beach washes away at tide and the refill it from the sand in the water. Kinda neat. Very relaxing beautiful blue clean beach. Lots of boating activity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A wonderful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The white sand, the clear water without weeds, no big waves, the ambiance with the bars boarding the beach... I really love this beach and intend to go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stoped to eat our lunch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We picked up a burrito near by and parked the golf cart to enjoy the beach.  Such a beautiful spot, quiet and serene.  The white sand and crystal blue water is just gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing stay!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really awesome beach area, crystal clear water, white sands, not too many people in the morning. Nice for long walks. We enjoyed it a lot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great free beach with warm, clear water. Bring your beach chairs and enjoy the day! We loved people watching. Everyone was having fun! This is a great family beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular Watee
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a gorgeous beach with the bluest water you'll ever see. Pictures don't even do it justice. Had a fun day exploring and ended on Playa Norte.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome neighborhood
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a very large group of family and friends staying all over the North end (Playa Norte) of Isla.  Really an awesome area that is safe and provides something to do for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the prettiest beaches I've seen.  Love the public access along the pricey hotel fronts. Pictures from the point were beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach! Lots of fun bars and restaurants to walk to. Feels safe, even at night. Would recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach with beautiful turquoise water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is seriously stunning. Dotted with palm trees and soft white sand it is a place where you can fully relax and enjoy the strong sun of Isla Mujeres. There are different sections of the beach- some have beach bars that play music and other stretches are peaceful and serene with only the sound of crashing waves. You get to choose what experience you want and there is something for everyone. There are beach vendors offering handmade bracelets etc  and massages but they are not overwhelming like some other places we’ve traveled to in the world. The water is clear and clean and isn’t very rough at all-perfect for swimming. Highly recommend this beach while visiting Isla Mujeres

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach from the whole Island. This is the beach that you must visit to relax and enjoy cold drinks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even if you are not staying on Playa Norte, make sure you spend a day on the beaches.  Good place to take sunset pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is amazing with white cool sands and warm crystal clear water. Definitely worth to spend a day on or even the whole vacation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Coast Line, Beaches and Crystal Clear Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Playa Norte for one day from Cancun and were so impressed that if we return to the region again we will stay on Isla Mujeres and specifically Playa Norte. The beaches are stunning and friendly, the water is calm and shallow (even out 25 metres), and the views are fantastic. Easy to get to, and lots of restaurants and bars are on the beach. A real highlight of our holiday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to Isla Mujeres for the day while staying in Cancun.  Made my way to Playa Norte which is a beautiful peaceful beach.  The water is blue and calm and you can got quite far out without it being too deep.  There are many places along the beach where you can rent a beach chair for the day.  There are bars and restaurants all along the beach and ladies come by offering massages and beach vendors offer their goods.  It is arelaxing place to spend the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Public Beach In All The Yucatan
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome beach, we spent all of our 7 days on Isla lounging here. We’ve come from Belize through Tulum and all up the Yucatan and this is the best beach we’ve seen. Even Cozumel didn’t come close as far as public beaches are concerned. There’s so much sand which is rare with all the erosion over the years and it extends 100 feet off the water at least. With plenty of natural shade in the form of palm trees, which are also perfect for setting up a hammock! The best part about it isn’t even the perfect blue shallow waters or the sandy bottom, it’s the fact that no one is bothering you! No hustling here at all. The odd person trying to sell mango or a massage but that’s it! You can choose to rent a bed at a beach club or you can choose to just chill. Amazing beach with lots to offer, Even some cool snorkelling over by the MIA Resort. Plan to spend lots of time here if you are downtown. Better yet, just stay downtown! Not a bad spot to catch the sunset either.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is a long stretch of sandy beach open to the public and within walking distance of the main town. The warm carribean waters are safe and shallow for a distance in to the sea.pleny of bars and hire of chairs and equipment are all available there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Golf buggy trip round the Island. Is absolutely devine there with beautiful beaches. A must see. Gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 4 years ago it was an amazing place - calm, beautiful white beach, some sunbeds - it was my paradise beach. But now it changed to a party zone without a possibility to relax. The beach was just cramed fully with of course rentable sunbeds so the beach seemed to be very small and even the part where it’s allowed to swim was very small. Loud and nasty music everywhere and big boats are just sailing a few meters from the shore. Much to near. The only thing that was still amazing was the crystal clear water but no chance for snorkeling this time - because of boats, jet ski and so on.When you like a Cancun - like Party come. If not go somewhere else. I was really disappointed. They sold this place. 😞

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been twice now and both times the beach was so crowded it sapped the fun out of it. The water is beautiful but right in front of you are many boats parked, enjoying the water. This further distracts from what should be a great view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Been hear many times, other beaches on island have gotten bad, but Norte looks cleaner every year. Sure you have to rent chairs and umbrellas but well worth is, water always calm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach ever
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have traveled a lot, and this is my favorite beach. It is crystal clear and calm. You can feed the fish and don't even need snorkeling equipment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to go from Cancun to the island by ferry, also the beach is not far from the port of the island for the ferry. The sand of the beach is very light and clean. I fall in love to super beautiful Carribean blue sea from the beach. Amazing time to me.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in Isla Mujeres
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach in Isla mujeres. The water are so clear and the color is just amazing. The beach may get a little crowded and yet, totaly worth visiting and even staying near by. It is very close to a street with lots of good resturants and souvenir shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gets busier every year
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome beach. Crowds are too much sometimes. Gorgeous sunsets. Hotels claim their piece of beachfront so you have to get there early or late.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great drinks and views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent our off day (non-diving or snorkeling) to visit the north end of the island on a golf cart.  Playa Norte was easy to find and provided beautiful views of the Caribbean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise away from home
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is the best beach in the island. Nice restaurants and good views of the sunset.  I will be back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quick Getaway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. White sand turquoise water friendly people.I'll be back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtakingly beautiful views while still experiencing local culture
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ventured to playa Norte from Cancun for the day with a friend that had been many times before, and throughly enjoyed the experience.  I was treated to a wonderful tour of the entire island via golf cart, and The views were absolutely spectacular!!  I loved venturing through the local family run restaurants offering their own specialties that were absolutely phenomenal!!!  The guacamole and Mexican salsa at La Lolita were the best I’ve ever had, and I’m a huge guac fan!   The mojito’s are delicious as well, and come served in wonderfully chilled stoneware, and served by very friendly staff... which is incredibly refreshing after a few hours on a golf cart.  Lol.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a must see if you are staying in cancun we took a ferry to isla mujeres for the day rented, gulf cars, and had lunch at a seafood restaurant. The water was crystal clear with no waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Place in Mexico.  Have been going there since 1996.  Always fantastic!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have met people here from all over the world.  They always say it is the only place in Mexico they would come back to.  Not the best for tourists or night life only because they are not open late, not because the music isn't incredibly diverse and comparable to anywhere else in Mexico you would go to.  Laid back, quiet nights.  AA+1 restaurants.  Stay away from the all inclusive hotels.  You want to experience the island, the people and the culture.  One of my favorite places is The Joint on the south end of the island.  Music in the morning, super friendly employees and great breakfast reasonably priced.  Unless you like bumpin' in the clubs and spring breakers this place is not for you.  Mature travelers preferred.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEST BEACH EVER!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at playa arena right on Playa Norte. We got out and explored the town as much as we could, but we felt like we were missing out by not being on the beach, so we wound up spending most of our time here. The sunrises and sunsets are incredible. The water is the most beautiful color I’ve ever seen. Of the 13 islands I’ve visited, this place is the most magical. Even the vendors are kind. A simple “No gracias,” kept them at bay and they were very kind and respectful. We made friends with several of them by doing this.I’ve seen people complain about boats, but the noise from the waves drowned out most music. Sundays seem to be the busiest. I loved seeing all the big boats and seeing others having a good time. We talked to a few of the passengers who came ashore. We paid the same price for our room for a night as what they paid for a six hour excursion! this was our first trip here, and as far as I’m concerned, it will be the only island I ever return to. It’s that awesome.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hounded by sellers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are more sellers than tourists on this island be warned you won't get a minutes peace, you are constantly badged by sellers. If you want a peaceful island visit go to Holbox.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vacation
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a wonderful week, swimming, snorkeling and enjoying the food. The weather was perfect, the friends that went with us had a great time too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you visit Isla Mujeres, walking along Playa Norte and watching the sunset is a must. Soft white sand, many places to eat and drink, chair and umbrella rentals are available for about $12 US (or less) all along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love coming here, whenever we have gone it has never been super crowded. Although at one time we did count 30 + boats out past the buoys, but the people tend to stay on or near those boats. We rented some chairs in front of Chimbos and Gabrielle was our waiter. What can we say, but he was awesome from the start! The bonus was when we went to leave he brought us a bucket of water and helped rinse the sand off of our feet! Talk about service. He always had a smile on his face and was super kind. We also like to visit the little massage place that has the green and pink curtain I think the color is. we have used Claudia and her gals several times. It was $35.00 for 70 mins.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We only visited for few hours during our catamaran trip, but, that was enough to leave a long lasting memory of this wonderful beach. We want to comeback and explore the area next time. Playa Norte is the Best Beach I ever visited!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful water, too many boats
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at Mia reef which is right next to playa Norte. We have visited various Caribbean beaches from Dominican Republic, Jamaica and Cozumel. The water is the best we have been in. Crystal clear water and very calm. Only drawback is that the beach is overrun with boats near the buoys on excursions from Cancun. The boats bring tons of people from about 10am to 6pm. The music blares from all the boats. When we are in the water before all the boats come it t pure heaven. The boats don’t completely ruin the experience but it does distract from the beauty of the waters.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice getaway, very nice place to visit and swim in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The actual part that you want to visit when checking out Playa Norte is not the section immediately next to the ferry landing. Keep going toward the Na Balam hotel. The area up there is very pristine, sandy and not as crowded. You can rent beach chairs and umbrellas for a couple hundred pesos. KIds will love swimming in the water. I don't think it gets deeper than four feet so you can wander out there and hang out. Lots of places to buy a beer and/or water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Couples Getaway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awww. What can I say. So relaxing. Clear blue waters. A lot to see and do. Enjoy your time and take it all in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite beach!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is beautiful.  The water is a perfect temperature, the sand is soft.  This is my happy peaceful place to go!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved playa norte from the first moment! The wite sand, the warm and clean water makes playa norte the paradise on earth!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in the qorld
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is stunning. It’s getting crowded. But if you go elsewhere on the island during the day and show up two hours before sundown you will have all the beauty with less crowds. Enjoy!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too many boats & people trying to sell
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful until all the boats from Cancun arrive after lunch. You can’t even see past 50 yards or so...it’s just boats, loud music and more boats. Forget laying back and enjoying a good book...every 5 minutes someone wants to sell you jewelry, henna, sarongs, shirts, peanuts, fruit, cigars, etc. I expect it when passing a shop...but not on the beach. It’s still one of the most beautiful beaches without the boats & sellers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a paradise! So beautiful beach, clean and white sand shallow sea. You can swim, puddle boarding, kayaking or snorkeling. Liked this little street where are so many cafes and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Sunset and friendly people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spend two evenings here watching the sunset. The view, sand and people were all the BEST.  Don't miss this free show.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrun!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What has happened to Isla??  We have been vacationing on Isla since 2002.  Have not been able to go 2017-2018 for various reasons.  We were SHOCKED at the change in the island.  North Beach now looks like a spring break beach in Florida. 30 + boats full of people from cancun pulling up everyday with music blaring and hundreds of people.  Day after day, all day long being bugged to buy jewerly, hammocks, wraps, tattoos(ps dont do this!! lasted 3 hrs not 3 weeks!! live and learn) massage, bracelets, nuts, headbands, hair braids, children selling candy,  "bands" begging for money after "playing something"?? We had money stolen from bag on beach.  Riding around the island on the golf cart is nearly impossible now d/t parts of the road dug out about every 8 feet.  They tried to fill it in with dirt but the are worse than ANY of the speed bumps.  Last but not least the prices have gone up to shocking levels for Isla!.  PS---fyi for smokers.  Isla turning into a no smoking island.  Sad sad sad!  Our little vacation spot is not recognizable!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset must
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Catch the end of the day here in warm waves and beautiful sand. Watch the sunset and stay in or out of the water just a bit longer for the beautiful skies. Unbelievable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Norte is the reason to come to Isla Mujeres! Beautiful white sand, NO SEAWEED!, and shallow blue water. Just perfect! Pay a few dollars to rent lounge chairs and enjoy your day. There are many food and drink options as well as inexpensive massages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are looking for a beach without the seaweed, this is the beach for you and your family. When you get off the ferry, just walk to the left. About 100 yards down the street, you will see rentals for golf carts. If you are interested in touring the island, the rental is well worth it, we loved it! If you are just interested in the beach, there are beach clubs all along the coast. The farther you walk, the less crowded it is. If you have small kids, the beach all the way at the end just in front of hotel MIA is the best. Crystal clear water and no more than thigh level deep for a long way out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I knew I’d love from my window seat in the plane!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As so many other reviewers shared, it is beautiful. Emerald and blue water tones. Yes, you can see the fish swimming around the water is so clear. The sand is white and soft. Highly recommend visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World class beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have visited Bali, Thailand and many other top beaches and punta norte is one of my top. There are many beachclubs where to relax, some more noisy than others so it is up to you.The water was cristal clear and there are no waves which makes it nice for kids too.There is an area for snorkling with loads of colorful fishes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach was beautiful...feed fish next to hotel mia..very relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach..water is warm...not very deep..fish swim.next to you bought saltine crackers feed the fish ...ecellent experience..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but CROWDED, shopping, shopping and more shopping.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful area downtown with lots of shopping choices and is SUPER CROWDED, but a must to visit anyway!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Never fails!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even on a cloudy day, this beach is beautiful. If you like to swim, you'll love this beach because you can essentially swim the length of it and see straight to the bottom. Sometimes it's busy, depending on the season, but even then it doesn't feel too crowded. You just have the find the right spot. We always go to the very end, near Hotel Mia.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: TOTAL DISAPPOINTMENT!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Saying Playa Norte is one of the top 10 beaches in the world is a joke! We arrived at Playa Norte and we didn't want to believe it! The beach is small and was completely crowded, the different beach bars were playing very loud music. Even worse were the 80 yachts moored a few meters from the beach, each playing music louder than the other !!! We thought we were going to paradise and ran into a fair !! A real nightmare !!Isla Mujeres and Playa Norte never again !!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vacationer trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is easy to spend the whole week enjoying Playa Norte. The sand is great and the water colors are superb.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get there early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get there before all the tour boats! it is beautiful always, but peaceful in the am! We got chairs next to Tarzan, much quieter and less people!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Getting SUPER Crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Have been to Isla many times and stay between Privileges & Ixchel.  This time I stayed at Privileges and several people staying there commented on how crowded it was.  I had no problem getting a spot on the beach though and really didn't notice the crowds.  However, next door at Ixchel it was horrible!!! Hundreds of people, you couldn't see the sand for all the people.  Both Ixchel and Privileges have "private" areas for their guests, but the beaches are public and anyone can use the beach.This trip I did see a lot of folks.  One family of about 20! was trying to camp out on Privileges property which security put a stop to.North Beach by Ixchel has better swimming as there is an artificial breaker that controls the current, at Privileges however, there is no barrier and the current drags you toward the pier.  You cannot just relax and float or swim, as you are always fighting the current. People literally clung to the barrier rope to keep from drifting off. Frustrating!Also, because of the artificial barrier, people tend to flock to the beach area by Ixchel.  I'm not sure how it is further down the beach and towards Mia which has a shallow bay.As for the crowds, I believe it has to do with the seaweed issue. I come back to Isla/Playa Norte because there is little to none.  The sunsets at Playa Norte are beautiful.While the beach is great, the crowds and in some places currents are an issue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach from Isla Mujeres
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The paradise exist, and his name is Playa Norte. You must visit, enjoy and relax on this beach. Take a cold drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely the best beach in isla Mujeres ! A good vibe in the center of everything. Restaurants kind of pricey but the beach is amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach but you have to get a sun bed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, shallow water that’s calm and easy to swim inRoped off swim areaBut v hot with no shade unless you rent a sun bed (ours was 100 mx each for the day) which included showers and loosLots of bars and restaurants nearbyIf you’re in the Isla Mujeres you’re not going to NOT go there are you?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice Beach. Fine sand, low buildings partially hidden by trees. Multiple facilities available. But super crowded and weed in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We ate at a local restaurant right on the beach. Playa Norte is quite fun, very lively and safe. A must stop destination for all while visiting Isla Mujeres.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An absolute must for children. The water represents more of a ‘bath tub’ feel vs. an ocean. It’s so beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Idyllic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, white sugar sand and turquoise warm waters. A beach lovers delight.Lovely beach bars nestled within the palm trees.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing beach destroyed by Cancun day trippers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is amazing, I've traveled the world and seen some amazing beaches, this is one of them. Crystal clear water, calm, white sand you can walk out hundreds of feet, even neck deep you can see your toes the water is so clear. Unfortunately, the idyll is shattered by dozens (literally, I've counted 30-40 at once) of boats that show up from Cancun starting around 10-11 am, blasting really REALLY loud music, each playing different music so what you hear on the beach is a cacophony, and staying until 4 or so in the afternoon. Get there early in the morning to enjoy it, or come back late afternoon and you can also catch an amazing sunset if the clouds cooperate.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Totally overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Isla Mujeres because we read that the beaches were absolutely amazing, especially Playa Norte. The water is warm, calm and a very clear turquoise. BUT, there’s a rope in the water where the swimming zone stops and the other side is basically a yacht parking lot. No view of the ocean, just the boats. And they all play different and super loud music, so much for a relaxing day at the beach. We couldn’t find an umbrella to purchase on the island, so unless you rent one, there is very little shade. We sat down next to a fence, where the sun was less brutal. We didn’t even take pictures, was not worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love Playa Norte
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach on Isla Mujeres. Clear water, nice people, relax, and cold drinks. You must visit Playa Norte, you will love it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The bluest waters I’ve ever seen. There are different restaurants and bars excellent to spend the day at.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best resort for Cancun - safe and very private with excellent food and amenities!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All inclusive experiences can be disapointing - but our stay here was simply superb! The restaurant offerings and the service was excellent and the dining areas were very comfortable and well maintained!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: More than beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cool breeze, sunlight and the coral beach.. it was a fabulous day out with my family. Everyone there looked so happy and satisfied with the whole atmosphere. Beach clubs are around and the music from them coming out.. I am definitely going back sooner or later

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I will admit, it’s really hot and more crowded than in the past but Playa Norte is really gorgeous. I love IM so I am biased. Hawaii is amazing, too, for that matter. But there is just something special about this island. There are no high rises or fancy resorts, so if those are your needs, go somewhere else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach of our trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water is absolutely crystal clear, zero seaweed whatsoever. Gentle waves and smooth sand. Rental umbrella/bench are good addition but not required for shorter stay, set up your own spot and go for a quick dip, the beach itself is free.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach overrun with people
